small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_HW configs (512, 1024) with num_warps=8/16 — H_out*W_out=3844 has plenty of work per (N,D_out) tile, and bigger tiles amortize the OC=16 weight loads better.
- The weight tensor is tiny (16*3*27=1296 floats = 5KB); preload it once into registers/SRAM outside the loops via a single `tl.load` of shape (OC, K_total) and index it, eliminating per-iteration scalar weight loads.
- Try grouping by N along program_id(1) only (drop D_out from grid) and looping D_out inside the kernel to reuse loaded x rows across depth — adjacent d_idx values share H/W gather patterns.
large_guidance:
- Reformulate as an explicit GEMM: tile (OC) × (BLOCK_HW spatial) with K=IC*KT*KH*KW=81 and use `tl.dot` with BLOCK_M=16 (OC), BLOCK_N=64–128, BLOCK_K=32 — this leverages tensor cores instead of the current outer-product FMA loop.
- Switch output layout to channels-last (N, D, H, W, OC) so the 16-wide OC store is contiguous, and use vectorized stores; the current store has stride DHW between OC channels which is uncoalesced.
- Make the kernel persistent over D_out: one program owns an (N, HW-tile) and sweeps all D_out depths, reusing the H/W gather indices and weight tile across depth iterations to cut redundant index math and weight broadcasting by D_out=14×.
